title: Contact-Aware Gear: neural-operator surrogate for spur-gear tooth stress under quasi-static frictional contact (code, datasets, trained models and result logs)
description:
Code, processed finite-element datasets, trained model checkpoints and result logs for a ten-member Fourier Neural Operator surrogate of the in-plane stress field in a spur-gear tooth under quasi-static frictional contact.

Version 3.2.0 adds a second finite-element model with a circular root fillet (0.38 modules, the ISO 53 profile A radius) and a three-tooth sector whose rim deforms and is fixed only at its bore. All 432 cases were solved with it (datasets v5 and v5f), and its 27 test cases were refined 1.5-fold and 2-fold: the labels change by 1.9% and 2.4% (5.6% and 7.4% for the sharp, clamped root), at an observed order of 1.3, and the largest root stress by at most 2.3%. A ten-member ensemble trained on v5f with the same protocol reproduces its labels to 0.9% and their peak root stress to 0.7%.

Version 3.1.0 builds the grid mask of the gear-mesh datasets from the finite elements of the tooth, retrains every network and adds robustness checks and matched baselines. Trained on 270 of 432 CalculiX solutions and tested on three held-out loading trajectories, the ensemble reproduces the finite-element field with a relative L2 error of 1.0% (R2 = 0.9999); over six trajectory-grouped partitions the error is 0.6% to 2.3%, and on six additional trajectories with unseen contact positions and approaches 1.9%. Refining every mesh length scale 1.5-fold and 2-fold changes the labels by 5.6% and 7.4%, so the accuracy describes agreement with the numerical model. The peak root tensile stress is predicted to 0.5%, and the change of the field with the friction coefficient is followed case by case. Under a matched tuning budget the FNO is more accurate than U-Net and a POD-DeepONet. One prediction takes 76 ms on a CPU against 27.1 s for a CalculiX solve.

This deposit contains the gearstress package; 70 dataset-generation, training, study, analysis and figure scripts; the test suite; the model-ready HDF5 datasets, including the corrected datasets v4 and v4f, the datasets v5 and v5f of the filleted-root model, the six additional test trajectories and the earlier datasets v1 to v3 used for method comparisons; every gear-mesh solution of both models on the prediction grid with its refined references at two further discretizations; 50 trained checkpoints, 20 behind the headline results, 10 trained on v5f and 20 on the earlier dataset v2; and the per-seed result logs of every run and the study summaries. The remaining checkpoints and the raw CalculiX output are available on reasonable request.

Source code is released under the MIT License; datasets, result logs and trained checkpoints under CC BY 4.0.
